<h2 id="about-title">About me</h2>

        <div class="about-grid">
          <figure class="about-photo"><img src="assets/home/atom-dodd-banner.jpg" alt="Atom Rosales teaching a workshop on data analysis, with the analysis projected behind him." width="1800" height="750" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Technical instruction &#183; DODD Short Courses</figcaption></figure>
          <div class="about-copy">
            <p class="about-lead">I entered mosquito control as a seasonal field technician in Texas. Setting traps, identifying mosquitoes, maintaining equipment, and coordinating field activities gave me an appreciation for how much public health decisions depend on the quality and context of the underlying data.</p>
            <p>My interest in GIS grew from wanting to solve practical problems that were difficult to understand from tables alone. One of my earliest GIS projects brought together a county storm sewer dataset and the locations of <em>Culex quinquefasciatus</em> mosquito pools that had tested positive for West Nile virus. By examining where positive-pool hotspots aligned with the storm sewer network, I used the existing infrastructure data to identify potential underground breeding sites and help plan a more focused surveillance and response strategy.</p>
            <p>That project showed me how geographic information could connect surveillance results to features in the environment and turn an observed pattern into a practical course of action. It led me further into GIS, programming, data visualization, and spatial analysis. Over time, my work expanded from organizing individual surveillance routes to developing organization-wide data systems, operational dashboards, aerial application analyses, and drone-based remote-sensing workflows.</p>
            <p>I later completed a graduate certificate in geographic information systems and a master's degree in spatial data science at Penn State. My education strengthened the analytical foundation behind work that has always remained grounded in field operations and applied public health.</p>

</div>
